title: ip.zscaler.com and the vendor's causes when traffic does not land on the nearest Public Service Edge
aliases: is my traffic going to zscaler
not going to nearest service edge

prose.text: ip.zscaler.com is the page that shows a device whether its traffic reaches the Zscaler service. {{ip-zscaler-com}}

prose.label: When the edge is not the nearest.
prose.text: How the nearest edge is chosen is in [[shared.cloud-architecture.service-edges]] and the variables in [[shared.pac-files.variables]]. {{gateway-name-dns-mismatch}} {{hardcoded-dc-ip}}

prose.label: Denylisted source IP.
prose.text: {{denylist-ip-check}} The vendor's performance test is in [[zia.troubleshooting.performance-testing]].

ip-zscaler-com.statement: To check if a user's traffic is going to the Zscaler service, go to ip.zscaler.com on the user's device. It shows the Zscaler cloud and the location of the Public Service Edge, the egress IP address and the virtual IP address of the Public Service Edge, the Zscaler hostname of the edge instance processing the traffic, the egress IP address of the network from which the edge receives traffic, and the IP address of the gateway. The page says the service might not recognize IPv6 traffic passing through the Zscaler cloud.

quotes: To check if a user's traffic is going to the Zscaler service, on the user's device, go to ip.zscaler.com.
The Zscaler cloud and the location of the Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA) to which your traffic is going
The egress IP address of the Public Service Edge
The virtual IP address of the Public Service Edge
The Zscaler hostname of the Public Service Edge instance that is processing your traffic
The egress IP address of the network from which the Public Service Edge receives traffic
The IP address of your gateway
Zscaler's My IP Address service (ip.zscaler.com) might not recognize IPv6 traffic passing through the Zscaler cloud.

denylist-ip-check.statement: Internet Access > Tools > Denylist IP Check shows whether the Zscaler service is placing service access from an IP address on the denylist due to suspicious traffic activity: a denylisted IP address is shown with additional comments, and otherwise there are no results.

quotes: You can check if the Zscaler service is placing service access from an IP address on the denylist, due to suspicious traffic activity.
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Tools > Denylist IP Check.
If the Zscaler service placed the IP address on the denylist, it displays the IP address with additional comments. If it didn't place the IP address on the denylist, then there are no results.

gateway-name-dns-mismatch.statement: When a PAC file uses gateway.<zscaler_cloud> (for example gateway.zscaler.net:80) and the DNS server is not in the same geographic region as the organization's Internet gateway location, the DNS server returns the IP address of the Public Service Edge in the data center closest to it, which might not be the closest to the user. Resolving whoami.akamai.net gives the IP address of the DNS server that resolved the Zscaler gateway name. The fix the article gives is ${GATEWAY}:80 for the primary proxy and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80 for the secondary.

quotes: The PAC file uses gateway.<zscaler_cloud> to define the Public Service Edge (for example, gateway.zscaler.net:80), and the DNS server is not in the same geographic region as your Internet gateway location.

When the DNS server receives a request to resolve the hostname, it returns the IP address of the Public Service Edge in the Zscaler data center that it is closest to, which might not be the closest Public Service Edge to the user.
You can determine the IP address of the DNS server that resolved the Zscaler gateway name by resolving the following hostname: whoami.akamai.net.
To resolve this issue, edit the PAC file and use ${GATEWAY}:80 for the primary proxy and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80 for the secondary proxy.

hardcoded-dc-ip.statement: Specifying the IP address of a Zscaler data center in a PAC file is not recommended, as it might cause problems when the user is remote and far from the Public Service Edge; the gateway-variable method is preferred because the service uses the GeoIP coordinates of the source IP address to determine the nearest Public Service Edge.

quotes: The PAC file specifies the IP address of a Zscaler data center. This is not recommended, as this might cause problems when the user is remote and is far from the Public Service Edge.
Edit the PAC file and use ${GATEWAY}:80 for the primary Public Service Edge and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80 for the secondary Public Service Edge.

The PAC file uses ${GATEWAY}:80 for the primary Public Service Edge and ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80 for the secondary Public Service Edge. This is the preferred method because the service uses the GeoIP coordinates of the source IP address to determine the nearest Public Service Edge.

ipv6-recognition.title: When ip.zscaler.com fails to recognize IPv6 traffic
ipv6-recognition.detail: The article says the My IP Address service might not recognize IPv6 traffic passing through the Zscaler cloud, without saying under what conditions or what the page then shows.
